hvik-01-c1.text: Judith Jesch (2017). What does the word ‘Viking’ really mean?. The Conversation.
hvik-01-c1.quote: In Old Norse, there are two words, both nouns: a víkingr is a person, while víking is an activity.
hvik-01-c1.claim: Old Norse had two related nouns: a víkingr was a person, while víking was an activity.

hvik-01-c1.text: Clare Downham (2017). Vikings were never the pure-bred master race white supremacists like to portray. The Conversation.
hvik-01-c1.quote: The word “Viking” entered the Modern English language in 1807, at a time of growing nationalism and empire building.
hvik-01-c1.claim: "Viking" entered Modern English in 1807, in an age of growing nationalism and empire

hvik-01-c2.text: Joanna Story. The Viking Raid on Lindisfarne. English Heritage.
hvik-01-c2.quote: On 8 June, heathen men came and miserably destroyed God’s church on Lindisfarne, with plunder and slaughter.
hvik-01-c2.claim: English Heritage dates the attack to 8 June

hvik-01-c3.text: Linda Koffmar (2020). Fallen in battle, these Swedish Vikings are part of a larger genetic puzzle. Uppsala University.
hvik-01-c3.quote: Four of the 34 men stacked on top of one another in the Salme II boat burial were full brothers.
hvik-01-c3.claim: showed that four of the men in Salme II were full brothers, and that the rest of the dead came from the same district

hvik-02-c1.text: Museum of the Viking Age (2026). The Oseberg Ship: Get to Know the World's Best-Preserved Viking Ship. Museum of the Viking Age, University of Oslo.
hvik-02-c1.quote: After 14 years at sea, the ship was hauled ashore for the last time and used as a burial ship for two women in the year 834.
hvik-02-c1.claim: After about 14 years at sea it was hauled ashore for the last time and became the burial ship of two women in 834.

hvik-02-c2.text: Emma Groeneveld (2018). Viking Ships. World History Encyclopedia.
hvik-02-c2.quote: With no saws in sight in northern Europe until the 13th century CE, Scandinavian craftsmen created planks by splitting tree trunks
hvik-02-c2.claim: With no saws in northern Europe until the thirteenth century, craftsmen split tree trunks instead

hvik-02-c3.text: Gábor Horváth, András Barta, István Pomozi, Bence Suhai, Ramón Hegedüs, Susanne Åkesson, Benno Meyer-Rochow, Rüdiger Wehner (2011). On the trail of Vikings with polarized skylight: experimental study of the atmospheric optical prerequisites allowing polarimetric navigation by Viking seafarers. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences.
hvik-02-c3.quote: This theory of polarimetric Viking navigation is accepted and frequently cited, in spite of a total lack of experimental evidence.
hvik-02-c3.claim: noted that it had been widely accepted and cited despite a total lack of experimental evidence

hvik-02-c3.text: Dénes Száz, Gábor Horváth (2018). Success of sky-polarimetric Viking navigation: revealing the chance Viking sailors could reach Greenland from Norway. Royal Society Open Science.
hvik-02-c3.quote: Our results show that the sky-polarimetric navigation is surprisingly successful on both days of the spring equinox and summer solstice even under cloudy conditions if the navigator determined the north direction periodically at least once in every 3 h
hvik-02-c3.claim: Dénes Száz and Horváth found sky-polarimetric navigation surprisingly successful even in cloudy weather, provided the navigator found north at least once every three hours.

hvik-03-c1.text: University of Bristol (2018). Radiocarbon dating reveals mass grave did date to the Viking age. University of Bristol.
hvik-03-c1.quote: One room was packed with the commingled remains of at least 264 people, around 20 percent of whom were women.
hvik-03-c1.claim: One room held the mixed bones of at least 264 individuals

hvik-03-c1.text: University of Bristol (2018). Radiocarbon dating reveals mass grave did date to the Viking age. University of Bristol.
hvik-03-c1.quote: New scientific research now shows that this was not the case and that the bones are all consistent with a date in the late 9th century.
hvik-03-c1.claim: Once it was corrected, every date fitted the late ninth century.

hvik-03-c2.text: Joshua J. Mark (2018). Rollo of Normandy. World History Encyclopedia.
hvik-03-c2.quote: Although Rollo is often referenced as the first Duke of Normandy, he never held that title (Richard II, his great-grandson, was the first duke).
hvik-03-c2.claim: Rollo is often called the first Duke of Normandy, but he never held that title: the first duke was his great-grandson Richard II.

hvik-03-c3.text: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle: Eleventh Century. The Avalon Project, Yale Law School.
hvik-03-c3.quote: This year was the payment of the tribute over all England; that was, altogether, two and seventy thousand pounds, besides that which the citizens of London paid; and that was ten thousand five hundred pounds.
hvik-03-c3.claim: In 1018 the whole country paid 72,000 pounds, plus 10,500 from the citizens of London

hvik-03-c3.text: Brandon M. Bender (2026). Cnut the Great: King of England, Denmark & Norway. World History Encyclopedia.
hvik-03-c3.quote: In the original version of the story, Cnut does this to demonstrate that he is not all powerful – only God is.
hvik-03-c3.claim: Cnut shows his flattering advisers that he is not all-powerful, because only God is.

hvik-04-c1.text: James E. Montgomery (2000). Ibn Faḍlān and the Rūsiyyah. Journal of Arabic and Islamic Studies.
hvik-04-c1.quote: they are Scandinavians, in particular the eastern Swedish tribe known by this name: a group of elite merchant-pirates operating out of Ladoga
hvik-04-c1.claim: The Rus could be Scandinavians, specifically an elite of eastern Swedish merchant-pirates operating out of Ladoga and Rurik's hill-fort.

hvik-04-c2.text: James E. Montgomery (2000). Ibn Faḍlān and the Rūsiyyah. Journal of Arabic and Islamic Studies.
hvik-04-c2.quote: Every day the slave-girl arrives in the morning with a large basin containing water, which she hands to her owner.
hvik-04-c2.claim: Every morning a slave girl carried a single basin of water round the house

hvik-04-c3.quote: Den bestod bland annat av 14 300 mynt och mängder av silverarmringar och armbyglar, där de yngsta mynten var präglade på 870-talet, med majoriteten från det islamiska Kalifatet.
hvik-04-c3.claim: It held about 14,300 coins and masses of silver arm rings and armlets; the youngest coins were struck in the 870s, and most came from the Islamic Caliphate.

hvik-04-c3.text: Mark Cartwright (2017). Varangian Guard: Bodyguard of the Byzantine Emperors. World History Encyclopedia.
hvik-04-c3.quote: by the 13th century CE, the majority of its members were English and the Guard used their own language when they acclaimed their adopted ruler.
hvik-04-c3.claim: after 1066 many Anglo-Saxons joined, and by the thirteenth century most of the guard was English.

hvik-05-c1.text: Magdalena M.E. Schmid, Andrew J. Dugmore, Orri Vésteinsson, Anthony J. Newton (2017). Tephra isochrons and chronologies of colonisation. Quaternary Geochronology.
hvik-05-c1.quote: These results suggest that although colonisation had started before the 870s in the southwest, the bulk of first settlement happened after that date.
hvik-05-c1.claim: colonisation had started before the 870s in the south-west, but the bulk of first settlement came after that date.

hvik-05-c2.text: Margot Kuitems, Birgitta L. Wallace, Charles Lindsay, Andrea Scifo, Petra Doeve, Kevin Jenkins, Susanne Lindauer, Pınar Erdil, Paul M. Ledger, Véronique Forbes, Caroline Vermeeren, Ronny Friedrich, Michael W. Dee (2021). Evidence for European presence in the Americas in AD 1021. Nature.
hvik-05-c2.quote: Our result of ad 1021 for the cutting year constitutes the only secure calendar date for the presence of Europeans across the Atlantic before the voyages of Columbus.
hvik-05-c2.claim: That makes 1021 the only secure calendar date for Europeans across the Atlantic before Columbus

hvik-05-c3.text: Boyang Zhao, Isla S. Castañeda, Jeffrey M. Salacup, Elizabeth K. Thomas, William C. Daniels, Tobias Schneider, Gregory A. de Wet, Raymond S. Bradley (2022). Prolonged drying trend coincident with the demise of Norse settlement in southern Greenland. Science Advances.
hvik-05-c3.quote: We find no substantial temperature changes during the settlement period but rather that the region experienced a persistent drying trend, which peaked in the 16th century.
hvik-05-c3.claim: reconstructed climate from the sediments of a lake beside a Norse farm and found no substantial temperature change during the settlement period

hvik-05-c3.text: Marisa Borreggine, Konstantin Latychev, Sophie Coulson, Evelyn M. Powell, Jerry X. Mitrovica, Glenn A. Milne, Richard B. Alley (2023). Sea-level rise in Southwest Greenland as a contributor to Viking abandonment. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
hvik-05-c3.quote: The results indicate that sea level rose up to ~3.3 m outside the glaciation zone during Viking settlement, producing shoreline retreat of hundreds of meters.
hvik-05-c3.claim: raised local sea level by up to about 3.3 metres, flooding coastal land and forcing people off many coastal sites.

hvik-06-c1.text: Thingvellir National Park. Lögberg. Thingvellir National Park.
hvik-06-c1.quote: The Law Speaker was chosen by the Lögrétta, the Legislative Assembly, for a three-year term and was the only paid employee of the Commonwealth.
hvik-06-c1.claim: The Law Speaker was chosen by the Lögrétta, the legislative assembly, for a three-year term and was the only paid official of the Commonwealth

hvik-06-c2.text: Charlotte Hedenstierna-Jonson, Anna Kjellström, Torun Zachrisson, Maja Krzewińska, Veronica Sobrado, Neil Price, Torsten Günther, Mattias Jakobsson, Anders Götherström, Jan Storå (2017). A female Viking warrior confirmed by genomics. American Journal of Physical Anthropology.
hvik-06-c2.quote: The genomic results revealed the lack of a Y‐chromosome and thus a female biological sex, and the mtDNA analyses support a single‐individual origin of sampled elements.
hvik-06-c2.claim: There was no Y chromosome: the warrior was a woman.

hvik-06-c2.text: Neil Price, Charlotte Hedenstierna-Jonson, Torun Zachrisson, Anna Kjellström, Jan Storå, Maja Krzewińska, Torsten Günther, Verónica Sobrado, Mattias Jakobsson, Anders Götherström (2019). Viking warrior women? Reassessing Birka chamber grave Bj.581 (online supplementary material). Antiquity.
hvik-06-c2.quote: every bone in the analysed skeleton is individually labelled 'Bj.581' in ink
hvik-06-c2.claim: every bone of the skeleton is individually labelled "Bj.581" in ink

hvik-06-c3.text: Emma Groeneveld (2018). Runes. World History Encyclopedia.
hvik-06-c3.quote: and in Sweden (c. 2600 stones) mainly focused in the provinces around Lake Mälaren
hvik-06-c3.claim: Sweden has about 2,600 Viking Age runestones, mainly in the provinces around Lake Mälaren

hvik-06-c3.text: Emma Groeneveld (2018). Vinland. World History Encyclopedia.
hvik-06-c3.quote: It has been suggested that Karlsefni and Gudrid's role has been magnified in this saga at the expense of Leif's, who is all but erased
hvik-06-c3.claim: Erik the Red's Saga may magnify Thorfinn Karlsefni and his wife Gudrid at Leif's expense, perhaps because a thirteenth-century movement sought sainthood for their descendant, Bishop Björn Gilsson.

hvik-07-c1.text: Museum of the Viking Age (2026). The Gjermundbu Helmet. Museum of the Viking Age, University of Oslo.
hvik-07-c1.quote: Viking battle helmets never had anything as impractical as horns.
hvik-07-c1.claim: Viking battle helmets never had anything as impractical as horns.

hvik-07-c1.text: Robert Kościelny (2022). Facts vs. fiction: How the real Vikings compared to the brutal warriors of lore. National Geographic.
hvik-07-c1.quote: One originating source for the horned helmets has been pegged: they were used by Carl Emil Doepler, the costume designer for the premiere of Wagner’s opera Ring of the Nibelung at the Bayreuth Festival in 1876.
hvik-07-c1.claim: costume designer for the premiere of Wagner's Ring of the Nibelung at the Bayreuth Festival in 1876

hvik-07-c2.text: Joshua J. Mark (2021). Viking Hygiene, Clothing, & Jewelry. World History Encyclopedia.
hvik-07-c2.quote: They combed their hair every day, bathed every Saturday, and even changed their garments often.
hvik-07-c2.claim: justifying the massacre of Danes in England in 1002, complained that the Danes made themselves too attractive to English women

hvik-07-c2.text: Robert Kościelny (2022). Facts vs. fiction: How the real Vikings compared to the brutal warriors of lore. National Geographic.
hvik-07-c2.quote: But the court doctor translated the phrase into Latin as ex craniis eorum quos ceciderunt—from the skulls of those they killed.
hvik-07-c2.claim: Worm translated the phrase into Latin

hvik-07-c3.text: St John's College, University of Cambridge (2020). World's largest DNA sequencing of Viking skeletons reveals they weren't all Scandinavian. ScienceDaily.
hvik-07-c3.quote: Two Orkney skeletons who were buried with Viking swords in Viking style graves are genetically similar to present-day Irish and Scottish people and could be the earliest Pictish genomes ever studied.
hvik-07-c3.claim: Two men buried with swords in Viking-style graves on Orkney were genetically similar to present-day Irish and Scottish people, and could be the earliest Pictish genomes yet studied.

hvik-07-c3.text: Linda Koffmar (2020). Fallen in battle, these Swedish Vikings are part of a larger genetic puzzle. Uppsala University.
hvik-07-c3.quote: Being a Viking was a cultural rather than genetic affiliation.
hvik-07-c3.claim: being a Viking was a cultural rather than genetic affiliation
